newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S COMBINED DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S COMBINED DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.

text.p: The women's combined downhill at the Alpine skiing world championships was called off on Thursday due to high, gusty winds exceeding 55 kph at the north Italian resort.
Organisers said that the championships could even stretch over to Sunday or Monday if the bad weather continued, although that remained a last resort option.
They re-scheduled the combined downhill for Friday at 0900 GMT and said Thursday's night slalom would go ahead as planned, weather permitting.
The downhill, scheduled for 1100 GMT on Thursday, had already been moved down to the super-G starting point but even there the wind buffeted safety netting and sent snow across the piste.
The start time was put back one hour but the winds failed to subside. Tom Winters, technical delegate for all women's Alpine events, said winds of up to 40 kph were usually acceptable.
"We're okay at 30-40 kph as long as it's not in big gusts and it's not dangerous off the jumps," said Winters. "We want to have a fair race for everyone."

The combined downhill was the first race at the championships to be hit by bad weather. Sestriere has until now been enjoying bright sunshine and perfect conditions and weather forecasts promise better weather for the weekend.
The setback recalled the past two world championships in Morioka, Japan, and Sierra Nevada in southern Spain, where wind and bad weather played havoc with the events.
Winters said that if the race could not be held on Friday either, it may be scheduled immediately after Saturday's regular women's downhill. A men's slalom is scheduled on Saturday night.
"It is a potential alternative course of action if we have to do it. But we haven't discussed it yet," said Winters.
"The combined must be a separate race in itself. In the past we have done a special downhill and immediately afterwards done a combined downhill.
"It would be a smaller field and very easy to put it on," he added. "Right now we're not looking out that far."
Only 26 starters from 14 countries had entered Thursday's event, by far the lowest number in Sestriere so far and the slalom is likely to further whittle down the field.
Some of the racers in the combined downhill had also only entered to get downhill practice and will not be able to take part now that it is after the slalom.
FIS general-secretary Gian-Franco Kasper said the regular women's downhill would have priority on Saturday or, if necessary, on the reserve day Sunday,
"If a race is not possible on those days, the jury may consider prolonging the championships to Monday," said Kasper.

"But it could also happen that there is no combined. It happened once before in Morioka," he added, referring to the 1993 championships when the men's super-G had to be scrapped because of the weather.
